'''David Walter Hafemeister''' (July 1, 1934 – March 31, 2023) was an American [[physicist]].

== Life and career ==
Hafemeister was born in [[Milwaukee, Wisconsin]], the son of Lester and Alma Hafemeister.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.legacy.com/us/obituaries/sanluisobispo/name/david-hafemeister-obituary?id=51844154|title=David Hafemeister Obituary (1934-2023)|work=[[The Tribune (San Luis Obispo)|The Tribune]]|date=May 10, 2023|access-date=May 31, 2026|via=[[Legacy.com]]}}</ref> He attended [[Northwestern University]], earning his [[Bachelor of Science|BS degree]] in [[mechanical engineering]] in 1957. He also attended the [[University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign]], earning his [[Master of Science|MS degree]] in 1960 and his [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD degree]] in [[physics]] in 1964.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://physics.calpoly.edu/dhafemei|title=David Hafemeister|work=[[California Polytechnic State University, San Luis Obispo]]|access-date=May 31, 2026}}</ref>

Hafemeister served as a professor in the department of [[physics]] at [[California Polytechnic State University, San Luis Obispo]] from 1972 to 2000. During his years as a professor, from 1975 to 1977, he worked as a science advisor in the [[United States Senate]],<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/The_Future_of_Land_Based_Strategic_Missi/PJf2jZbIPjcC?hl=en&gbpv=0|title=The Future of Land-Based Strategic Missiles|page=IX|editor=Hobson, Art. Goss Levi, Barbara. Sakitt, Mark|date=June 1989|publisher=American Inst. of Physics|ISBN=9780883186190|via=[[Google Books]]}}</ref> and in 1988, he was named a [[List of fellows of the American Physical Society|fellow]] of the [[American Physical Society]], "for continuing contributions to the analysis of science and society issues relating to energy and the nuclear arms race".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/funding-recognition/aps-fellowship?q=hafemeister&af=true|title=APS Fellow Archive|work=[[American Physical Society]]|access-date=May 31, 2026}}</ref>

== Death ==
Hafemeister died in [[San Luis Obispo, California]] on March 31, 2023, at the age of 88.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.illinoisalumnimagazine.org/illinoisalumni/summer_2023/MobilePagedArticle.action?articleId=1889284#articleId1889284|title=In Memoriam|work=Illinois Alumni Magazine|date=2023|access-date=May 31, 2026}}</ref>
